solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Preserved food appropriate after party

indicators.note: after places the word for appropriate behind the party, as the charade's order

parts.note: CON is the abbreviation for the Conservative Party
fit means suitable or appropriate

explanation.surface: A tin of preserved food is brought along once the party is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Confit is meat, typically duck, slow-cooked and kept sealed in its own fat, a classic preserve.

clue.text: Middle of statue gilded, it's suggested — Cicero, say?

indicators.note: gilded means coated in gold all round, so gold letters enclose the middle

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry; gilding is suggested by gold on both sides

indicators.note: Middle of takes the central letters of the word statue

explanation.surface: A statue of Cicero is apparently covered in gold leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is heraldic gold; gilding is implied by gold on each side, OR AT OR, the AT being the middle two letters of statue.
explanation.definitionFit: Cicero was the great public speaker of ancient Rome, an example of the definition, hence 'say'.

clue.text: I, Adam?

definitions.meaning: I is the ... pronoun in grammar
Adam, in Genesis, was the first human

explanation.walkthrough: The grammatical term and Adam's place in Genesis share the same two words.
explanation.definitionFit: 'I' is the pronoun of the speaker in grammar, while Adam was humanity's original man in the Bible.

clue.text: Rock found in ideal pudding served up in restaurant

indicators.note: found in places the rock inside the other letters
served up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI in crosswords
a tart is a pastry pudding
a tor is a rocky peak or outcrop

explanation.surface: A stone turns up in a perfect dessert at a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reads the ideal pudding upwards as TRATIA; 'found in' sets the rock inside. 'Ideal' as A1 is a crossword convention, written AI.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is an informal Italian eating place, a kind of restaurant.

clue.text: A saint corrupted, and saint becoming sinner?

indicators.note: corrupted suggests the letters of the phrase are spoiled and twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A holy person goes bad and turns from saint to sinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupted' rearranges A SAINT into SATANI; the question mark admits that a devil-worshipper is only one example of a sinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A devil-worshipper is, from a church viewpoint, an archetypal wrongdoer, so an example of the definition.

clue.text: Maximum taken in drink, spit it out!

indicators.note: taken in means the maximum is held inside the word for drink

parts.note: to sup is to drink
a peak is the highest point or maximum

explanation.surface: Someone at the bar is urged to talk after drinking the most possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spit it out' looks like an order about the drink; it means 'say it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are urgings to say what one has to say, out loud and clearly.

clue.text: Subject almost ripe then?

indicators.note: almost means the final letter is cut from the phrase

parts.note: fruit that is ripe is ready to pick

explanation.surface: Asking whether a fruit is nearly ripe enough.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the theme or matter under discussion.

clue.text: Fruit lover

definitions.meaning: a ... is an enthusiast, as in a fitness ...

explanation.definitionFit: Botanically a nut is a dry fruit, and informally the word means a fan or devotee.

clue.text: Fifteen from London run without clothes

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here, the word for without dressing the run

parts.note: sans is a word for without
a race is a run

explanation.surface: Someone from London streaks, running without any clothes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is a verb, the word for without dressing the run. Saracens is a rugby union club in north London; a rugby side has fifteen players.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby union team has fifteen players, and Saracens is a London club.

clue.text: Legitimate target in coconut shy, possibly?

definitions.meaning: a person or thing it is acceptable to attack or criticise
a coconut shy, where balls are thrown to knock down coconuts, is a game at a fair

explanation.surface: Something is fair to aim at, like the coconuts at a funfair stall.
explanation.walkthrough: A coconut shy is a British fairground stall where you throw balls to knock coconuts off posts.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names anyone open to attack, while the literal phrase describes an amusement played at a funfair.

clue.text: Taper lit up, designed primarily for small explosive

indicators.note: lit up is slang for drunk, so the letters of the word taper reel into a new order
primarily means the opening letter of the word designed is used

explanation.surface: A burning taper is used to light a little bomb built for the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lit up' rearranges TAPER into PETAR; 'primarily' takes the D of 'designed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A petard was a small bomb used to blast through gates or walls, as in being hoist with one's own.

clue.text: After tango, miss catching heel of cabaret singer

indicators.note: After puts the rest behind the letter for tango, as the charade's order

parts.note: T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: catching means the word for miss holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: to omit is to miss out or leave out

indicators.note: the heel is the back end, so the last letter of cabaret

explanation.surface: Following a tango, a woman stumbles and snags the heel of a cabaret performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' puts T, the last of cabaret, into OMIT to give OMTIT. 'Miss' and 'singer' look human; one is a verb, the other a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The tomtit, a small titmouse, is a songbird, so a singer in crossword terms.

clue.text: Ready for a good turn, foul defender

parts.note: to kick an opponent is a foul in football
a back is a defending player in football or rugby

explanation.surface: A footballer is primed to do a good deed, then fouls a defender instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is British slang for cash (ready money), not 'prepared'.
explanation.definitionFit: A kickback is an illicit payment made in return for a favour, so money handed over for a good turn.

clue.text: Gift opened by the scoundrel, one for Gordon Bennett

indicators.note: opened by means the gift is split for the other letters to go inside

parts.note: a boon is a gift or blessing
a rat is a scoundrel
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A present is unwrapped by a rogue, one meant for a man named Gordon Bennett.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gordon Bennett!' is a British exclamation of exasperation, not a person here.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild cries of annoyance, so the exclamations are interchangeable.

clue.text: Corn loaf good, far from soft?

parts.note: an ear is the seed-bearing head of corn
a split tin is a British loaf baked in a tin and cut along the top

explanation.surface: A baker's order: corn, a good loaf, and nothing too soft.
explanation.walkthrough: A split tin is a common British bread loaf. 'soft' is the musical sense, quiet, not soft bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Ear-splitting noise is extremely loud, the opposite of quiet, which is what soft means in music.

clue.text: Dummy run in a mo, using bombing

indicators.note: in places the letter for run within the shuffled letters
bombing suggests the letters are blasted apart and land in a new order

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A practice run is done in a moment, using bombs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bombing' rearranges the letters after 'in' into IGNOAMUS, and 'in' sets the run letter inside. 'Dummy run' reads as one phrase but splits after the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dummy is an informal word for a stupid person, as is ignoramus.

clue.text: God inspired by prayer a lot

indicators.note: inspired by means breathed in, so the god goes inside the prayer

parts.note: a plea is an appeal or prayer
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A deity motivated by a great deal of praying.
explanation.definitionFit: A plethora is an excess or abundance, a great deal of something.

clue.text: Tea in angel's cup different — though in essence it's the same

definitions.text: though in essence it's the same

indicators.note: in places the word for tea inside the rearranged letters
different signals that the letters of angel's cup are made into something else

parts.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: Tea served in a heavenly cup tastes different, though really it is just the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges ANGELS CUP to PLUSCANGE, and 'in' puts CHA inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The French saying 'the more things change, the more they stay the same' observes that apparent change is superficial.

clue.text: Swine painting Henry, satirical cartoonist

parts.note: a hog is a pig or swine
painting is a kind of art
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A pig painted by Henry, the satirist.
explanation.definitionFit: William Hogarth was an 18th-century English artist famed for satirical prints such as Gin Lane.

clue.text: Screw: one's sheared off

definitions.meaning: to screw someone is to swindle or overcharge them
the wool shorn from a sheep

explanation.walkthrough: 'Screw' is slang for cheat, not the fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleece means to swindle, and also names the coat of wool that shearing removes.

clue.text: Fetid coloured liquid entering wound

indicators.note: entering means the liquid goes inside the word for wound

parts.note: a sting is a small wound, as from a bee
ink is a coloured liquid for writing

explanation.surface: A foul-smelling stained discharge seeps into an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something that reeks, smelling rank and offensive.

clue.text: China: a little souvenir, a miniature turned up

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means read from bottom to top
a little means only part of the run of words is taken

explanation.surface: A small porcelain keepsake, a tiny ornament, upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little' takes IRAMI from souvenIR A MIniature and 'turned up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Imari is Japanese porcelain, so a type of china.

clue.text: So concerned with partner

parts.note: re means regarding or concerning
an ally is a partner or associate

explanation.surface: Someone worries about their partner a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both work as intensifiers: 'so tired' and 'really tired' say the same thing.

clue.text: Greeting cat, who's barking

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters of these words go crazy into a new order

explanation.surface: Saying hello to a cat that seems to be barking like a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' (British for mad, as in barking mad) rearranges CAT WHO.
explanation.definitionFit: Wotcha is an informal London hello, a worn-down form of the old salutation 'what cheer'.

clue.text: Plastic fish

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means fake or mock, like something plastic

explanation.definitionFit: Cod as a modifier means sham or imitation, as in cod philosophy; it is also a well-known sea creature.

clue.text: Around US state, Marxist stayed

indicators.note: Around means the word for Marxist goes round the state

parts.note: a red is a communist or Marxist
Maine is a state in the north-east of the USA

explanation.surface: A communist hung about somewhere in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain is to stay put, so the past tenses are synonyms.

clue.text: Type of course where golf played

definitions.meaning: a ... course is a British degree with a year of work placement in the middle
... in Kent hosts Royal St George's, an Open Championship golf links

explanation.surface: Asking what kind of golf course is played somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are British: a sandwich course splits study around work experience, and Sandwich is a Kent town with a famous links.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an education term, the other a place name known for its championship golf course.

clue.text: Lighter and firm dip at the end of the day?

definitions.text: dip at the end of the day?

parts.note: the sun is what lights the world, so a lighter
set means firm or solid, as a jelly sets

explanation.surface: A cigarette lighter and a firm dip, perhaps snacks for the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' looks like a cigarette lighter and 'dip' like a sauce; the dip is the sun sinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunset is when the sun sinks below the horizon in the evening, a daily descent.
